title: Simple Greeting Function
description: Write a C program that defines a function named `greet`. This function should not accept any arguments and should not return any value. When called, it should print a greeting message.
constraints: The `greet` function must be `void` and take no parameters. It must be called from `main`.
explanation: The greet function is called and prints a greeting.

title: Sum Function with Return Value
description: Define a C function named `add`. This function should take two integer arguments and return their sum as an integer. In your `main` function, prompt the user to input two integers, call `add`, and print the result.
constraints: The `add` function must take two `int` parameters and return an `int`. Input integers will be between -1000 and 1000.
sampleOutput: The sum of the two numbers is: 40
explanation: The two integers are read, their sum is computed and printed.

title: Cube Calculator Function with Prototyping
description: Create a C function named `calculateCube` that takes a single integer `num` as input and returns its cube as an integer. Use a function prototype before `main`, then call the function from `main` after reading user input.
constraints: Input integer will be between 1 and 10 (to ensure the cube fits within a standard `int`).
explanation: The cube of 4 is computed by the function and printed.

title: Check Even/Odd Using a Boolean-like Function
description: Implement a C function named `isEven`. This function should accept one integer argument. It should return `1` if the number is even, and `0` if the number is odd. In your `main`, read a number, call `isEven`, and print 'Even' or 'Odd'.
constraints: Input integer will be between -1000 and 1000.
explanation: The isEven function returns 0 for 7, so 'Odd' is printed.

title: Simple Power Function (No Math Library)
description: Write a C function named `power(base, exponent)` that calculates the `base` raised to the power of `exponent`. The base will be an integer and the exponent will be a non-negative integer. Do not use the math library.
constraints: Base: 1 to 10. Exponent: 0 to 5. The result of the power calculation must fit within a standard `int`.

title: Prime Number Checker Function and Generator
description: Refactor the logic for checking if a number is prime into a reusable C function named `isPrime(int num)`. Then, for a given input N, print all prime numbers up to N.
constraints: N will be an integer between 2 and 50 (to limit computation for typical interactive testing).
explanation: All primes <= 20 are found with isPrime and printed.

title: Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) Function
description: Implement a C function named `findGCD(int a, int b)` that calculates the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) of two positive integers using the Euclidean algorithm.
constraints: Input integers `a` and `b` will be positive, between 1 and 1000.
explanation: The GCD of 48 and 18 is computed with the Euclidean algorithm.

title: Factorial Calculation (Recursive Function)
description: Reimplement the factorial calculation using a recursive C function named `factorial(int n)`. The function should define a base case and the recursive case.
constraints: Input `n` will be an integer between 0 and 12 (to ensure the result fits within a standard `int` type and avoids overflow).
explanation: factorial(6) is computed recursively and printed.

title: Understanding Call by Value vs. Call by Reference
description: Write a C program that declares an integer variable `myNum` and initializes it to 5 in the `main` function. Define a separate function `modifyValue(int num)` that takes an integer parameter and sets it to 10. Print the value of `myNum` before and after calling `modifyValue` to demonstrate call by value.
constraints: None. The problem is designed to demonstrate a concept.
sampleOutput:
Initial value of myNum: 5
Value of myNum after calling modifyValue: 5
explanation: Passing by value means changes in the function do not affect the original variable.

title: Unit Conversion Functions for Length and Weight
description: Create a C program that acts as a simple unit converter. Define two functions: `float metersToFeet(float meters)` and `float kgToPounds(float kg)`. Prompt the user for a length in meters and a weight in kilograms. Print the converted values.
constraints: Input values for meters and kg will be positive floating-point numbers between 0.0 and 1000.0.
sampleOutput:
10.00 meters is equivalent to 32.81 feet.
5.00 kg is equivalent to 11.02 pounds.
explanation: Meters and kg are converted using the specified factors and printed.
